A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UNIKIE-BENCH work. All 22 pages, including equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.10, are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 15 LMMs on two KIE tracks in Tables 4–5, alongside faithfulness, authenticity, diversity, and attention analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and analyses, with revised constrained-category results in Table 4.

M1.justification: The schema-guided extraction formulation, document reconstruction and annotation pipelines, and inference prompt remain unchanged. Newly disclosed annotator qualifications do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 4,472 constrained-category documents across 11 scenarios and 1,661 open-category documents across four document types and two languages. Dataset sources and coverage in Tables 1, 2, and 6 are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 evaluate the same 15 LMMs, and Appendix A.5 retains the same authenticity evaluators. Gemma's reordered rows and Table 7's new group headings do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The reported exact-match field-level F1 metric, image-size limit, unified prompt, temperature setting, and model identifiers remain unchanged. No revised protocol is reported to explain the Table 4 score changes.

E4.justification: The faithfulness and error analyses in Sections 5.2–5.3, authenticity and diversity analyses in A.5, attention analysis in A.8, and document case studies in A.9 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point estimates and authenticity counts without adding repeated-run information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Numerical revisions do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 substantially revises the central constrained-category results for 14 of 15 models, changing some rankings. Claude-Sonnet-4.5's commercial score changes from 56.73 to 45.92, and SmolVLM2-2.2B's advertisement score from 11.18 to 27.16. GLM-4.1V-9B overtakes GPT-4o on average. Gemini-3-Pro's row, Table 5 scores, and appendix findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same task definitions and Equations (1)–(3). No mathematical assumptions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two-track benchmark contribution and claims about persistent difficulties with diverse schemas, long-tail fields, complex layouts, and visual grounding.

C2.justification: Interpretations of performance differences, faithfulness, attention behavior, and extraction failures remain unchanged. The limitation to single-page or short-document settings is also retained; the ethics rewrite adds no substantive scientific limitation or mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendix A.10 newly discloses that the three annotators held master's degrees, had 1–3 years of enterprise KIE experience, and were proficient in Chinese and English. Annotation workflows, hardware, model identifiers, prompts, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, comparison with prior benchmarks in Table 3, and research positioning remain unchanged. Reference-page differences result from text reflow.

P1.justification: V2 refines several headings, rewrites Ethical Considerations, adds Acknowledgments, and lightly edits Appendix A.9. These are localized revisions; the main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 7 gains closed-source/open-source group headings, and Gemma rows move in Tables 4 and 7. Bold emphasis on the best average scores is removed from Tables 4–5. Figure 7's caption changes, page numbers disappear, and some text reflows; figure content remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Annotator qualifications in A.10 and clearer grouping in Table 7 provide modest documentation gains. However, the substantial Table 4 score revisions have no accompanying explanation or validation under the unchanged reported protocol. The PDFs do not establish whether this central empirical evidence became more accurate, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
